gaps.old_draft_snippet: However, the mechanism is inherently polarization-selective: only one circular polarization state couples efficiently to the desired output channel, halving the theoretical maximum diffraction efficiency at approximately 25% for unpolarized illumination.
gaps.scientific_content: The specific quantitative limit on diffraction efficiency for geometric phase metasurfaces under unpolarized illumination (approx. 25%), resulting from the inherent polarization selectivity where only one circular polarization state couples efficiently.

gaps.old_draft_snippet: Titanium dioxide (TiO2) metasurfaces fabricated by electron-beam lithography have demonstrated diffraction efficiencies exceeding 75% in the visible range, substantially outperforming comparable gold-based plasmonic structures limited by absorption losses.
gaps.scientific_content: Specific performance metrics for dielectric metasurfaces, namely TiO2 achieving >75% diffraction efficiency in the visible spectrum via electron-beam lithography, and the comparative disadvantage of gold-based plasmonic structures due to absorption losses.

audit.notes: The new blocks describe the mechanisms qualitatively but omit two key scientific details present in the old draft: 1) The specific 25% efficiency cap for geometric phase under unpolarized light, which is a critical design constraint. 2) The specific efficiency benchmark (>75%) for TiO2 metasurfaces compared to plasmonic alternatives, providing a concrete performance baseline for dielectric platforms.
